document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  const toc = document.querySelector(".main-toc");
  if (!toc) return;

  const links = Array.from(toc.querySelectorAll('a[href^="#"]'));

  const sections = links
    .map(link => {
      const id = link.getAttribute("href").replace("#", "");
      const section = document.getElementById(id);

      return section
        ? {
            id: id,
            link: link,
            section: section
          }
        : null;
    })
    .filter(Boolean);

  if (!sections.length) return;

  function setActive(activeLink) {
    links.forEach(link => {
      link.removeAttribute("aria-current");
      link.classList.remove("is-active");
    });

    activeLink.setAttribute("aria-current", "location");
    activeLink.classList.add("is-active");
  }

  function updateActiveLink() {
    let currentSection = sections[0];

    /*
      This controls when the TOC changes.
      0.35 means the active section changes when the section reaches
      about 35% down from the top of the viewport.
    */
    const activationPoint = window.innerHeight * 0.35;

    sections.forEach(item => {
      const sectionTop = item.section.getBoundingClientRect().top;

      if (sectionTop <= activationPoint) {
        currentSection = item;
      }
    });

    const nearBottom =
      window.innerHeight + window.scrollY >= document.documentElement.scrollHeight - 10;

    if (nearBottom) {
      currentSection = sections[sections.length - 1];
    }

    if (currentSection) {
      setActive(currentSection.link);
    }
  }

  let ticking = false;

  function onScroll() {
    if (!ticking) {
      window.requestAnimationFrame(function () {
        updateActiveLink();
        ticking = false;
      });

      ticking = true;
    }
  }

  updateActiveLink();

  window.addEventListener("scroll", onScroll, { passive: true });
  window.addEventListener("resize", updateActiveLink);

  links.forEach(link => {
    link.addEventListener("click", function () {
      setTimeout(updateActiveLink, 300);
    });
  });
});
</script>

What is Alabama Medicaid Provider Enrollment?

settings.editor: Alabama Medicaid provider enrollment is the process by which physicians and other healthcare practitioners register with the Alabama Medicaid Agency so they can order, refer, prescribe, or bill services for Medicaid recipients in the state. Federal law requires this enrollment before a provider can participate in the program. Contracting Providers manages the full process on your behalf, including documentation review, portal submission through the Alabama Medicaid provider enrollment system, follow-up with the state agency, and status tracking through to approval.
What's typically included: Application preparation, document collection, Alabama Medicaid portal submission, state agency follow-up, status tracking, and re-enrollment support.
Typical timeline: 60 to 90 days depending on provider type and state processing volume.

settings.title: What's Included in Our Alabama Medicaid Provider Enrollment Services

settings.editor:
Alabama Medicaid provider enrollment is not a single form or a one-time submission. The Alabama Medicaid Agency operates its own portal and documentation requirements, and providers must meet those standards before gaining approval to bill Medicaid patients in the state. For solo physicians and group practices managing this process internally, the administrative burden is significant, and the most common result is an avoidable delay caused by choosing the wrong enrollment type or submitting incomplete documentation.

Contracting Providers handles the full enrollment workflow for Alabama providers, from the first document review to active status confirmation with the Alabama Medicaid Agency.

settings.editor: From intake to active enrollment status, here is how Contracting Providers manages your Alabama Medicaid provider enrollment from start to finish.

settings.title: Provider Intake and Document Collection (Days 1 to 5)

settings.editor: We start by identifying the scope of your Alabama Medicaid enrollment. This includes confirming whether you are enrolling as an individual provider, a group, or both, and how many providers need to be enrolled. We collect your credentials, licensure, malpractice coverage, NPI information, and any existing CAQH data. Our team reviews everything for completeness before moving forward. Incomplete submissions are the leading cause of enrollment delays in Alabama, and we eliminate that risk upfront.

settings.title: Enrollment Type Selection and CAQH Setup (Days 3 to 10)

settings.editor: One of the most common mistakes providers make when attempting Alabama Medicaid enrollment on their own is selecting the wrong enrollment type. We identify the correct type before any application is submitted. Simultaneously, if you do not have an active CAQH ProView profile, we build it from scratch. If one exists, we audit it for accuracy and complete any outstanding attestation requirements.

Our specialists prepare your application for the Alabama Medicaid Agency and submit through the appropriate portal. All documentation is tailored to meet Alabama-specific requirements. We log confirmation of receipt and begin tracking status immediately after submission.

We track your application status and follow up directly with the Alabama Medicaid Agency. If additional documentation is requested or an issue arises, we handle it without requiring you to manage the back-and-forth. We continuously check status throughout the process to keep your enrollment moving.
Once enrollment is confirmed by the Alabama Medicaid Agency, we deliver your Medicaid provider ID and enrollment confirmation documentation. We flag your revalidation date so nothing lapses.

settings.editor: Alabama Medicaid is administered by the Alabama Medicaid Agency, a state agency that operates independently of the federal Medicaid framework while following CMS guidelines. There is no single national portal. Providers must complete enrollment directly through the Alabama Medicaid Agency before they can bill for services rendered to Medicaid recipients in the state. Federal law requires that physicians and other practitioners who prescribe, order, refer, or bill services for Alabama Medicaid recipients be enrolled as Medicaid providers. This applies to both individual providers and group practices.

settings.title: How Alabama Medicaid Provider Enrollment Works

settings.editor: When a provider enrolls with the Alabama Medicaid Agency, they are registering at the fee-for-service level. This is the foundational enrollment step. After state fee-for-service enrollment is confirmed, providers who want to participate with Alabama Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs) must complete a separate credentialing and enrollment process with each MCO individually. These are two distinct processes, and MCOs will not begin their review until the state enrollment is confirmed.

Choosing the wrong enrollment type is the most common mistake Alabama providers make when attempting to enroll on their own. The Alabama Medicaid Agency requires providers to select the correct enrollment category based on provider type, specialty, and billing structure. An incorrect selection results in a denial that requires starting the process over. Our team confirms the correct enrollment type before any application is submitted.

The Alabama Medicaid Agency interfaces with CAQH ProView as a primary source for provider data. An expired CAQH attestation, which requires re-attestation every 120 days, can trigger rejection of a pending Alabama Medicaid application. Contracting Providers monitors attestation schedules for every provider we work with to prevent this from happening.

Federal law requires Alabama Medicaid providers to revalidate their enrollment periodically. Missing a revalidation deadline results in automatic disenrollment. The provider can no longer bill Medicaid until re-enrollment is complete. Our team tracks revalidation dates and initiates the process in advance of deadlines to prevent any gap in enrollment status.

settings.title: Enrollment is completed through the Alabama Medicaid Agency provider enrollment portal. Providers must select the correct enrollment type before submission. An incorrect selection results in a denial and requires restarting the process.

After state Medicaid fee-for-service enrollment is confirmed, providers who want to bill through Alabama Medicaid managed care plans must enroll separately with each MCO operating in the state. These MCO enrollments run on independent timelines and involve their own credentialing processes. Contracting Providers coordinates MCO enrollment following state approval so providers achieve full billing access as efficiently as possible.

Every Alabama Medicaid application requires a valid National Provider Identifier. For group practices, a Type 2 NPI is required in addition to each rendering provider's Type 1. Taxonomy codes must accurately reflect the provider's specialty. Mismatched taxonomy codes are a common cause of rejections and can set a provider back four to six weeks.

Contracting Providers is not the Alabama Medicaid Agency. We help healthcare providers prepare, manage, and complete payer enrollment and credentialing tasks, including Alabama Medicaid provider enrollment support. The Alabama Medicaid Agency controls all final enrollment decisions and approvals.

settings.editor:
Alabama Medicaid provider enrollment and provider credentialing are closely linked but distinct processes. Enrollment grants a provider the right to bill the Alabama Medicaid Agency for fee-for-service claims. Credentialing verifies that the provider meets the clinical and professional standards required by the Alabama Medicaid program and its managed care organizations.

Most Alabama Medicaid MCOs require credentialing as a condition of in-network participation, even after state enrollment is complete. Without credentialing, a provider may be enrolled at the state level but unable to bill through the managed care organizations that serve the majority of Alabama Medicaid beneficiaries.

settings.editor: Credentialing through an Alabama Medicaid MCO typically takes 60 to 120 days from initial application submission. Delays occur most commonly due to incomplete applications, outdated CAQH data, or unresolved primary source verification issues. Contracting Providers front-loads the process with a pre-submission audit to minimize avoidable delays.

A provider who completes state enrollment but has not yet been credentialed by the relevant Alabama MCOs may face a gap period during which claims are denied. Our team coordinates enrollment and credentialing timelines simultaneously to reduce or eliminate that gap.
